## Summary

HTC was founded in 1997 by Cher Wang and H. T. Cho (the infobox also
names Peter Chou), is
listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange and is headquartered in Taoyuan,
Taiwan [1]. It began as an original design manufacturer of laptops,
then built phones for Palm, Fujitsu-Siemens, Hewlett Packard, Google
and Sony Ericsson, including the Nexus One and the Pixel, before
selling Android phones under its own name; in 2015 it unveiled the
Vive VR headset with Valve [1]. In January 2018 Google completed the
purchase of roughly half of HTC's design and research staff for US$1.1
billion [1]. The IEEE registry lists 29 MA-L blocks to "HTC
Corporation", all at No. 23 Xinghua Road, Taoyuan [2].

A MAC in an HTC block is most likely an HTC or HTC-built Android phone,
or a Vive headset [1]. The HTC U12+, announced in May 2018, runs on a
Snapdragon 845 [4]. Android 10 and later uses a persistent randomized
MAC per network by default, so only newer HTC phones would hide the
burned-in address [5]. In February 2013 HTC settled FTC charges that it
failed to take reasonable steps to secure the software on millions
of HTC devices, citing
the Carrier IQ and HTC Loggers logging tools and permission bypasses
[3]. Radio details and FCC grantee codes are not listed: the FCC ID
databases refused the session that wrote this entry, and nothing is
filled in from memory.
